kinds.instruction: Do not propose. You are shown both the documented rules and the source. Read this cycle's executions beside the proposals: for each expectation that failed, say whether the proposer misread the rule, or the rule as written and the code part company; quote the rule's words and name the line of code. Say which failures matter and what a proposer should try next. Cite blocks by id.
kinds.title: Criticism

kinds.instruction: You are shown the documented rules of the checks, not their code, and ONE cell of a grid under 'The cell to cover'. The cell names a relation between the cited span and the document, and a relation between the value and the span. The input is one JSON object with the three string fields value, span and document, written out in full, standing in exactly the relations the cell names; keep the document one short sentence and write a line break inside a field as \n. The rewritten text is the same object with the cell's named differences removed: the document rewritten so that the span occurs in it character for character, and the value rewritten so that it is a run of characters inside the span, character for character. If the cell names no difference on either side, change the value instead by one letter so that it is no longer inside the span. Say what the rule, read as written, says the check's answer ought to do: move or stay. Your expectation comes from the rule's words alone: name in the body the words you read it from, and say which verdict the rule gives before and after. Your kernel is conformance.kernel.grounding or conformance.kernel.span-occurs. The commitments are a STRING whose content is JSON of the form {"kernel": "<id>", "input": "<the input text>", "rewritten": "<your rewritten text>", "expect": "moves" or "unchanged", "rewrite": "<one sentence naming what you changed>", "cell": "<the cell exactly as named>"}. The input and the rewritten text are instances written out in full, never descriptions. Do not repeat a pair shown among the earlier proposals.

port_types.header: The documented rules of the checks

problem: The checks under test are the conformance harness's own functions. Most seats are shown only their documented rules, not their code: how the harness recovers a JSON object from a reply, whether it had to recover it from prose, its response verdict, its refusal-phrase check, and its grounding matcher. The question: is there an input and a rewrite of it on which the rule, read as written, says one thing and the check, run by machine, does another? The executor runs the check on both texts and records what its answer did; nothing here decides anything, the record shows where a reading and the machine parted.
